paragraph: Garfield runs on multi-family. Thirty-two two- and three-family sales over six months at a median of $767,125, with 78 percent closing above asking, a sale-to-list ratio of 1.047, and a 20-day median days on market. That is a real seller's market, and it reflects buyers who can count rental income toward qualifying, which pushes what they can pay past what a single-family buyer would stretch to. Detached single-family sold 21 times at a median of $565,000, also with 81 percent above asking and 20 days on market, so sellers there are dictating terms too. Condos and townhouses are the quieter tier: 10 sales, a median of $525,000, a sale-to-list ratio right at 1.00, and 35 days on market. Priced right, they move, but they are not drawing the same bidding pressure. The monthly numbers are too thin to read a trend, with several months under five closings in each category, so the six-month picture is the honest guide. If Garfield follows the usual Bergen seasonal arc, expect closings and medians to ease as fall arrives. If you're comparing tiers, the deciding factor isn't market heat. It's whether you want the space of a single-family, the rental income of a multi-family, or the low-maintenance lifestyle of a condo.
